Performing K-Nearest Neighbors vs. Naive Bayes on Binary and Multiclass datasets.

##Naive Bayes
data_processing.R ran in this code to ensure .Rmd file can run smoothly.
```{r}
#Loading training set data
binary_train <- read.csv("~/Downloads/binary_train.csv")
multiclass_train <- read.csv("~/Downloads/multiclass_train.csv")
binary_test <- read.csv("~/Downloads/binary_test.csv")
multiclass_test <- read.csv("~/Downloads/multiclass_test.csv")

#Initially run the data_processing.R code to prep for scaling datasets
 library(caret)


# Identify the feature type from the data setidentify_feature_types

identify_feature_types <- function(data) {
  
  numeric_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  
  binary_cols <- c()
  continuous_cols <- c()
  
  for (col in numeric_cols) {
    unique_vals <- unique(data[[col]])
    unique_vals <- unique_vals[!is.na(unique_vals)]
    
    if (length(unique_vals) == 2) {
      binary_cols <- c(binary_cols, col)
    } else {
      continuous_cols <- c(continuous_cols, col)
    }
  }
  
  
  return(list(
    binary = binary_cols,
    continuous = continuous_cols
  ))
}

# -----------------------------
# Fit scaler for Training data
# -----------------------------
fit_scaler <- function(train_data, continuous_cols) {
  
  scaler <- preProcess(
    train_data[, continuous_cols],
    method = c("center", "scale")
  )
  
  return(scaler)
}

# -----------------------------
# Transformation the data
# -----------------------------
transform_data <- function(data, scaler, continuous_cols) {
  
  data_scaled <- data
  
  data_scaled[, continuous_cols] <- predict(
    scaler,
    data[, continuous_cols]
  )
  
  return(data_scaled)
}

# -----------------------------
# Data pipeline 
# -----------------------------
  prepare_data <- function(train_data, test_data) {
  
  # Step 1: Identify feature types
  feature_types <- identify_feature_types(train_data)
  
  feature_types$binary
  feature_types$continuous
  cat("Binary Features    : ",feature_types$binary, "\n")
  cat("Continuous Features: ",feature_types$continuous, "\n")
  
  continuous_cols <- feature_types$continuous
  
  # Step 2: Fit scaler ONLY on training
  scaler <- fit_scaler(train_data, continuous_cols)
  
  # Step 3: Transform both datasets
  train_processed <- transform_data(train_data, scaler, continuous_cols)
  test_processed  <- transform_data(test_data, scaler, continuous_cols)
  
  return(list(
    train = train_processed,
    test = test_processed,
    scaler = scaler,
    feature_types = feature_types
  ))
  }

#Onto scaling 

#Scaling binary dataset
binary_result <- prepare_data(binary_train, binary_test)
binary_train_scaled <- binary_result$train
binary_test_scaled <- binary_result$test

#Scaling multiclass set 
multiclass_result <- prepare_data(multiclass_train, multiclass_test)
multiclass_train_scaled <- multiclass_result$train
multiclass_test_scaled <- multiclass_result$test

binary_target <- "Diabetes_binary"
multiclass_target <- "Diabetes_012"

# Convert targets to factors
binary_train_scaled[[binary_target]] <- as.factor(binary_train_scaled[[binary_target]])
binary_test_scaled[[binary_target]] <- as.factor(binary_test_scaled[[binary_target]])

multiclass_train_scaled[[multiclass_target]] <- as.factor(multiclass_train_scaled[[multiclass_target]])
multiclass_test_scaled[[multiclass_target]] <- as.factor(multiclass_test_scaled[[multiclass_target]])

#Applying SMOTE to handle class imbalances
library(ROSE)
set.seed(12)
binary_train_balanced <- ROSE(Diabetes_binary ~ ., data = binary_train_scaled, p = 0.5, seed = 123)$data

#Performing Gausian Naive Bayes on Binary
library(e1071)
set.seed(12)
nb_binary <- naiveBayes(Diabetes_binary ~ ., data = binary_train_balanced)
nb_binary.pred <- predict(nb_binary, binary_test_scaled)
nb_binary.prob <- predict(nb_binary, binary_test_scaled, type = "raw")

#Evaluate
library(caret)
cm_binary <- confusionMatrix(nb_binary.pred, binary_test_scaled$Diabetes_binary, positive = "1")
print(cm_binary)
#Get resulting confusion matrix and statistics analysis

# Store metrics
nb_binary_metrics <- data.frame(
  Model = "Naive Bayes (Balanced)",
  Accuracy = cm_binary$overall["Accuracy"],
  Precision = cm_binary$byClass["Precision"],
  Recall = cm_binary$byClass["Sensitivity"],
  F1 = cm_binary$byClass["F1"],
  Specificity = cm_binary$byClass["Specificity"]
)

#Naive Bayes Gaussian on Multiclass Dataset
nb_multiclass.fit <- naiveBayes(
  Diabetes_012 ~ .,  # Target is 0,1,2
  data = multiclass_train_scaled
)

nb_multiclass.pred <- predict(nb_multiclass.fit, multiclass_test_scaled)
nb_multiclass.prob <- predict(nb_multiclass.fit, multiclass_test_scaled, type = "raw")

#Evaluate
cm_multiclass <- confusionMatrix(nb_multiclass.pred, multiclass_test_scaled$Diabetes_012)
print(cm_multiclass)

# Calculate macro F1
nb_macro_f1 <- mean(cm_multiclass$byClass[, "F1"], na.rm = TRUE)

nb_macro_f1 <- mean(cm_multiclass$byClass[, "F1"], na.rm = TRUE)

#Using numeric indices
nb_multiclass_metrics <- data.frame(
  Model = "Naive Bayes",
  Accuracy = cm_multiclass$overall["Accuracy"],
  Macro_F1 = nb_macro_f1,
  Class0_F1 = cm_multiclass$byClass[1, "F1"],  # First class
  Class1_F1 = cm_multiclass$byClass[2, "F1"],  # Second class
  Class2_F1 = cm_multiclass$byClass[3, "F1"]   # Third class
)

print(nb_multiclass_metrics)
```


```{r}
library(class)
set.seed(12)
#K-NN on Balanced Binary Dataset
train.X.balanced <- binary_train_balanced[, !names(binary_train_balanced) %in% "Diabetes_binary"]
train.Direction.balanced <- binary_train_balanced$Diabetes_binary
test.X <- binary_test_scaled[, !names(binary_test_scaled) %in% "Diabetes_binary"]
test.Y <- binary_test_scaled$Diabetes_binary

#Testing K = 3, 5, 7, 11, 15
k_values <- c(3, 5, 7, 11, 15)
balanced_results <- data.frame()

for(k in k_values) {
  set.seed(1)
  knn.pred <- knn(train.X.balanced, test.X, train.Direction.balanced, k = k)
  cm <- confusionMatrix(knn.pred, test.Y, positive = "1")
  
  balanced_results <- rbind(balanced_results, data.frame(
    K = k,
    Accuracy = cm$overall["Accuracy"],
    Precision = cm$byClass["Precision"],
    Recall = cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],
    F1 = cm$byClass["F1"],
    Specificity = cm$byClass["Specificity"]
  ))
}
  print(balanced_results)

best_k_balanced <- balanced_results[which.max(balanced_results$F1), "K"]
best_f1_balanced <- max(balanced_results$F1)

cat("\n Best K for BALANCED data:", best_k_balanced, 
    "with F1 =", round(best_f1_balanced, 4), "\n")

# Store best KNN binary results
knn_binary_metrics <- balanced_results[balanced_results$K == best_k_balanced, ]
knn_binary_metrics$Model <- paste("KNN (K=", best_k_balanced, ")", sep="")
```
##K Nearest Neighbors

```{r}
library(class)
#Multiclass KNN Balanced 
train.X <- multiclass_train_scaled[, !names(multiclass_train_scaled) %in% "Diabetes_012"]
train.Y <- multiclass_train_scaled$Diabetes_012
test.X <- multiclass_test_scaled[, !names(multiclass_test_scaled) %in% "Diabetes_012"]
test.Y <- multiclass_test_scaled$Diabetes_012

#Testing K = 3, 5, 7, 11, 15
multiclass_results <- data.frame()

for(k in k_values) {
  set.seed(1)
  knn.pred <- knn(train.X, test.X, train.Y, k = k)
  cm <- confusionMatrix(knn.pred, test.Y)
  
  # Calculate macro F1 (average across classes)
  macro_f1 <- mean(cm$byClass[, "F1"], na.rm = TRUE)
  multiclass_results <- rbind(multiclass_results, data.frame(
    K = k,
    Accuracy = cm$overall["Accuracy"],
    Macro_F1 = macro_f1,
    Class0_F1 = cm$byClass[1, "F1"],  # First class
    Class1_F1 = cm$byClass[2, "F1"],  # Second class
    Class2_F1 = cm$byClass[3, "F1"]   # Third class
  ))
}

print(multiclass_results)

# Best K based on macro F1
best_k_multiclass <- multiclass_results[which.max(multiclass_results$Macro_F1), "K"]
best_macro_f1 <- max(multiclass_results$Macro_F1)

cat("\n Best K for MULTICLASS:", best_k_multiclass, 
    "with Macro F1 =", round(best_macro_f1, 4), "\n")

# Store best KNN multiclass results
knn_multiclass_metrics <- multiclass_results[multiclass_results$K == best_k_multiclass, ]
knn_multiclass_metrics$Model <- paste("KNN (K=", best_k_multiclass, ")", sep="")
```

##KNN Sensitivity
Binary and Multiclass Results using ggplot2
```{r}
#KNN Sensitivity Binary Results
library(ggplot2)

binaryKNN_plot <- ggplot(balanced_results, aes(x = K, y = F1)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 4) +
  labs(title = "KNN Sensitivity Analysis - Binary Classification",
       x = "Number of Neighbors (K)",
       y = "F1 Score") +
  theme_minimal()

print(binaryKNN_plot)

#KNN Sensitivity Multiclass Results
library(ggplot2)

best_k_multi <- multiclass_results$K[which.max(multiclass_results$Macro_F1)]
best_macro_f1 <- max(multiclass_results$Macro_F1)

multiclass_plot <- ggplot(multiclass_results, aes(x = K, y = Macro_F1)) +
  geom_line(color = "purple", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(color = "purple", size = 4) +
  geom_point(data = multiclass_results[multiclass_results$K == best_k_multi,], 
             aes(x = K, y = Macro_F1), 
             color = "red", size = 6, shape = 8) +
  labs(title = "KNN Sensitivity Analysis - Multiclass Classification",
       subtitle = paste("Best K =", best_k_multi, "| Macro F1 =", round(best_macro_f1, 4)),
       x = "Number of Neighbors (K)",
       y = "Macro F1 Score") +
  theme_minimal()

print(multiclass_plot)

if(nb_binary_metrics$F1 > knn_binary_metrics$F1) {
  binary_winner <- "Naive Bayes"
} else {
  binary_winner <- "KNN"
}

#Binary NB vs KNN Comparison
cat("\n BINARY CLASSIFICATION:\n")
cat("\nNaive Bayes (Balanced):")
cat("\n  Accuracy:", round(nb_binary_metrics$Accuracy, 4))
cat("\n  Precision:", round(nb_binary_metrics$Precision, 4))
cat("\n  Recall:", round(nb_binary_metrics$Recall, 4))
cat("\n  F1 Score:", round(nb_binary_metrics$F1, 4))

cat("\n\nKNN (K =", best_k_balanced, "):")
cat("\n  Accuracy:", round(knn_binary_metrics$Accuracy, 4))
cat("\n  Precision:", round(knn_binary_metrics$Precision, 4))
cat("\n  Recall:", round(knn_binary_metrics$Recall, 4))
cat("\n  F1 Score:", round(knn_binary_metrics$F1, 4))

#Multiclass NB vs KNN Comparison
cat("\n\n MULTICLASS CLASSIFICATION:\n")
cat("\nNaive Bayes:")
cat("\n  Accuracy:", round(nb_multiclass_metrics$Accuracy, 4))
cat("\n  Macro F1:", round(nb_multiclass_metrics$Macro_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 0 F1:", round(nb_multiclass_metrics$Class0_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 1 F1:", round(nb_multiclass_metrics$Class1_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 2 F1:", round(nb_multiclass_metrics$Class2_F1, 4))

cat("\n\nKNN (K =", best_k_multiclass, "):")
cat("\n  Accuracy:", round(knn_multiclass_metrics$Accuracy, 4))
cat("\n  Macro F1:", round(knn_multiclass_metrics$Macro_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 0 F1:", round(knn_multiclass_metrics$Class0_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 1 F1:", round(knn_multiclass_metrics$Class1_F1, 4))
cat("\n  Class 2 F1:", round(knn_multiclass_metrics$Class2_F1, 4))

#Metric Comparison Table
binary_baseline_acc <- max(table(binary_test_scaled$Diabetes_binary)) / nrow(binary_test_scaled)

comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Binary", "Binary", "Binary", "Multiclass", "Multiclass", "Multiclass"),
  Model = c("Baseline", "Naive Bayes", paste("KNN (K=", best_k_balanced, ")", sep=""),
            "Baseline", "Naive Bayes", paste("KNN (K=", best_k_multiclass, ")", sep="")),
  Accuracy = c(binary_baseline_acc, 
               nb_binary_metrics$Accuracy, 
               knn_binary_metrics$Accuracy,
               0.3333,  # Random guess for 3 classes
               nb_multiclass_metrics$Accuracy,
               knn_multiclass_metrics$Accuracy),
  F1_Score = c(0,
               nb_binary_metrics$F1,
               knn_binary_metrics$F1,
               0.3333,
               nb_multiclass_metrics$Macro_F1,
               knn_multiclass_metrics$Macro_F1)
)

print(comparison_table)

comparison_long <- data.frame(
  Model = rep(comparison_table$Model[2:3], 2),
  Metric = c(rep("F1 Score", 2), rep("Accuracy", 2)),
  Score = c(comparison_table$F1_Score[2], comparison_table$F1_Score[3],
            comparison_table$Accuracy[2], comparison_table$Accuracy[3])
)

comparison_plot <- ggplot(comparison_long, aes(x = Model, y = Score, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
```
